title: deferred-ack credit duplication from partial-commit fast-path
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Under certain transient network conditions and leader handoff paths, a deferred-ack fast-path causes the rate engine to record ephemeral 'credits' that are never reconciled. These fabricated credits allow brief quota overage windows for impacted API keys and routes, leading to underbilling and bursty throttling anomalies when the system later reconciles. This issue appears during partial-commit acknowledgements from an async write pipeline (commit->ack mirror) where the write leader returns success before all downstream shards have durably applied the debit. The read path and metric aggregator consume the partial state and increment available balance for the key, producing a short-lived duplication of credits.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a small multi-shard dev cluster with leader + 2 replicas and enable async commit fast-path (feature-flag: async-commit-fastpath)
2) Configure a test API key with a per-key burst quota and short window (10 requests / 1s) and route-based metering enabled
3) Drive concurrent requests from a load generator to exhaust the quota while simultaneously introducing packet loss between leader and one replica (tc/netem drop 20% on replica link)
4) Observe metric aggregator ingest stream: some commits are acked by leader before replica apply; aggregator sees the accepted commit and increments credits due to an early reconciliation heuristic

5) After briefly recovering network, leader reconciles durable state and replays; the credits originally issued are not withdrawn, causing a transient over-allow window and then a corrective burst of rejections when reconciliation completes
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between async-commit-fastpath flag and incidence of ghost credits in staging logs (rate_engine module trace) - spike at 2026-02-24T14:12:30Z
Metric aggregator uses 'accepted' event stream rather than durable 'applied' stream for near-real-time accounting; this optimization conflates leader-acked-without-apply events under partition
Race happens because commit-id is assigned and returned before durable apply ACK from majority; some downstream systems index the commit early and treat it as final
KV cache / prefix-caching interacts: prefix eviction triggered on reconciliation path sometimes re-adds tokens when seeing early accepted events

Repro steps validated in local harness with synthetic packet loss. Root cause narrowed to two components: early-accept ingestion path + lack of tombstone/reversal when durable apply fails or is delayed
proposed_solution: Short-term mitigation (hotfix): change metric-aggregator to prefer 'applied' stream; if not available, tag 'accepted' events with leader-seen flag and do not credit until a follow-up durable-apply confirmation or a safe timeout expires

Permanent fix: implement durable-confirmation window in rate-engine where credits are provisional until apply confirmation; on durable-apply mismatch, perform a compensating debit operation with idempotency keys to avoid double-charge
Update leader to delay client-visible success for commits affecting billing-critical events OR provide explicit two-phase ACK semantics for billing events (fast-path opt-in with opt-out flag)
Add reconciliation worker that scans recent accepted-vs-applied deltas and issues compensating adjustments with audit logging and customer-visible reasons
rollout_plan: 1) Implement hotfix in metric-aggregator (branch: eng/ENG-888210/agg-provisional) and run unit+integration tests
2) Deploy hotfix to staging cluster behind feature-flag (agg-prefer-applied) and run chaos tests (packet loss scenarios) for 48 hours
3) If stable, roll the aggregator hotfix to canary subset of production (10% of traffic) for 24 hours and monitor billing deltas and throttling patterns
4) Deploy permanent change (provisional credits + reconciliation worker) in next minor release (runtime-1.22.1) behind kill-switch and enable progressively
5) Notify CS/Accounts about potential historical underbilling window and prepare remediation script if needed
qa_checks: E2E test harness that simulates leader-replica lag and verifies no net increase in available credits after recovery
Property-based tests for idempotent compensating debits using commit-id and reconciliation-run-id
Integration smoke to assert aggregator only increments committed balance after durable-apply confirmation or expiry of provisional window
Load test with 50k requests/min to ensure no latency regression in aggregation path when provisional credits are blocked
monitoring_playbook: Immediate metrics to watch: provisional_credits_issued, reconciled_compensations, per_key_burst_success_rate, rejected_after_reconcile_count
Create dashboard 'ENG-888210: forgiveness window' showing accepted_vs_applied_streams, derived_bill_delta, and tail latency of commit->apply
Alert if reconciled_compensations > 5/min for more than 5m (P0)
On alert: enable agg-prefer-applied flag, escalate to oncall infra, run reconciliation job to re-evaluate recent 10m window, and contact affected customers via CS if persistent
